verdict.rationale: ComplyAdvantage has some of its own rule-driven automation. Users can configure the risk-score equation, and onboarding runs AML screening based on the resulting risk score, so a configured rule drives an automatic action on a customer event. Selectable screening configurations add a little more control. There is no evidence of a general rules engine for defining event-to-action rules, and webhooks (including WORKFLOW_COMPLETED) only send event notifications rather than providing rule-defined actions. Missing for 10: a documented user-defined rules/automation engine, configurable triggers across event types, configurable actions beyond risk-based screening (e.g. auto-assign or auto-escalate cases), and independent or hands-on corroboration.
